About

I'm an electrical engineer, and I'm at my best when a project touches both the circuit board and the code. For two years at Gannon University I worked with Prof. Wookwon Lee, the ECE Department Chair, building a cyber-physical systems framework for a 1/5th-scale autonomous vehicle.

That meant doing a bit of everything — designing and 3D-printing parts, soldering and tracing PCB faults, wiring up GPS and sensors, running ROS on Linux, and actually taking the vehicle outside to see how it held up. Away from the vehicle, much of my research has been in DC microgrids and renewable energy.

Selected Work

Research & projects

PROJECT 01 · FLAGSHIP

CPS Framework — 1/5th-Scale Autonomous Vehicle

My two-year graduate project with Prof. Wookwon Lee: a full cyber-physical systems platform on an off-road chassis. I designed and 3D-printed the compute box and chassis parts, tracked down the PCB wiring faults that kept crashing it, integrated GPS and stereo cameras, and ran the vehicle through outdoor field tests on a ROS/Ubuntu stack. The platform became the testbed for our IEEE CCNC 2026 paper on sAV/sUAS video-based navigation.

PROJECT 02

Bidirectional DC-DC Converter for DC Microgrids

I built a droop-controlled converter to balance power between solar, battery, and load. It held voltage steady at 98% as loads changed, and tuning the MPPT pushed energy harvest up 65% in simulation.

MATLABSimulinkDroop controlMPPT
PROJECT 03

Secure IoT Communication System

I designed an encrypted channel so sensor data could move safely between edge devices and base stations, without anyone listening in.

IoTEncryptionEmbedded
PROJECT 04

Power Shoe — Energy Harvesting

A wearable prototype that turns the energy from your footsteps into electricity — a fun dive into piezoelectric and mechanical harvesting.
